Guidance & outlook: We expect retail to be INR10,000 crores business this year.
It is exactly this best of execution that gives us the confidence to reaffirm our operating EBITDA guidance of INR7,000 crores to INR7,700 crores of FY27.
It is around 30% in FY27, roughly 40% in '28 and around 30% in FY29, which is milestone gated, ROCE and ROE accretive and backed by strong order visibility.
Growth & demand: Our module volumes sold during the quarter grew 89% over the prior period from 1.9 gigawatts to 3.6 gigawatts.

Our total order book has grown from approximately INR47,000 crores at end of FY25 to INR53,000 crores last financial year and now INR61,500 crores as on 2 8th of July 2026, taking our total order book of module in gigawatts terms to 25.2 gigawatts.

If we look at the order book also, like this quarter, we have added a substantial order book and largely on account of the DCR-driven order book as well as the export order book, when we see the realization for this order book also, the realization still ranging between USD0.24, USD0.25 for next couple of quarters.
Margins & costs: First, raw material costs rose globally driven by the metal indices and price movement out of China, and that compressed margin across our industry, and we were not immune.
Operating EBITDA came in at INR1,440-odd crores, up 44.4% year-on-year at an operating EBITDA margin of 18.2%.
Our profit after tax for the quarter stood at INR892 crores, up 15.4% year-on-year at a margin of 11%.
Capex & expansion: On the capacity, we commissioned an additional 3 gigawatt of module capacity at our SMS plant, Samakhiali, Gujarat in April '26 Waaree Energy Storage Solutions commenced the automated BESS container production at 5.15 gigawatt hours, nearly 1.5x the 3.5 gigawatt hours we had originally planned.

WRTL completed the acquisition of an approximately 55% stake in Associated Power Structures for approximately INR1,225 crores, extending our reach decisively into transmission and distribution and separately won a 1.5 gigawatt in our BESS EPC orders and signed the early contractor involvement agreement for utility scale solar plus BESS project in Australia a…
Our modules in India capacity stands at 24.2 gigawatts running at an annualized utilization of around 50% this quarter.
Balance sheet & cash: And on our return ratios, we continue to run a net cash balance sheet with a net debt to equity of minus 0.08x as on 30th of June, an ROCE of 28.5% and ROE of 24.8%.

We already have our largest module capacity outside of China, a track record of expanding ahead of competition, scale that act as a moat, driving procurement advantages, operating leverages and bankability.
In terms of the cash flow, like quarter one itself, our operating cash flow has been far better because of controlled inventory that has continued.
Risks & challenges: Second, our export mix were softer as some shipments and clearances took longer than we would have liked.
Every quarter of rapid growth brings its own challenges.
We are not just deploying capital in one large risky way.

Guidance & outlook: I want to highlight that our reported total EBITDA of INR 6,617 crores has surpassed our guidance range which has given earlier INR5,500 crores to INR6,000 crores worth of financial year '26, which reflects the strength and consistency of our execution.

Our integration across the entire energy value chain, along with structural demand, is expected to expand total addressable market by 4x, from approximately $1 trillion today to approximately $4 trillion by 2035.
The global solar inverter market is currently approximately $16 billion annually and is expected to grow at roughly 11% CAGR over the next dec ade, reaching approximately $46 billion by 2035.
Growth & demand: This time across the full fiscal year, our revenue from operations in this year has recorded a growth of approximately 84% year -on-year, reaching INR26,537 crores.
Operating EBITDA grew 117% to INR5,909 crores with an operating EBITDA margin of 22.27%.
Our order book continues to remain robust to approximately INR53,000 crores.
Margins & costs: Glass accounts approximately 20% plus of our module cost and one of the most critical components in the module quality, efficiency, durability, and yes, the cost.
Operating EBITDA came in at INR5,908.64 crores, registering a growth of 117% with margins improving to 22.27% versus 18.84% in the previous financial year.
Operating EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR1,576 crores, up by 70% margins.
Capex & expansion: Our Board has approved a capex of INR3,900 crores PV glass manufacturing for capacity of 2,500 TPD.
On the capacity side, we have commenced construction of our 10-gigawatt ingot wafer facility at Nagpur, which is with a capex of INR6,200 crores.

At Waaree, we have a current transformer capacity of around 4,000 MVA and we are adding up another 16,000 MVA of capacity, taking a total of 20,000 MVA in the current financial year, with a capex outlay of around 192 crores at our Alwar facility in Rajasthan.
Balance sheet & cash: We have maintained a debt -to-equity ratio of less than one, despite heavy capex cycles for nearly a decade.
Our strong last -mile access through our installers and franchise network gives us the ability to influence customer decisions at the point of sale, and the channel leverage is enormous.
So, if you look at our cash flow statement also, you are pointing out very right that the cash flow operations percentage has significantly come down.
Risks & challenges: Our total commitment in this segment stands at INR3,250 odd crores, and we are building a de-risked value-driven IPP portfolio for our marquee clients, which creates long -term order visibility across all the manufacturing segments within the group.
Sequentially, if I look at, there is a INR7000 crores of order decline.
But the margin impact has been very severe this quarter, 590 bps decline.
